text:
nora: Quick sync re: promotion of tenant Y to eu-west. Ops ran a dry-run and hit a huge idempotency map blowup for one hot tenant. Need a strategy to avoid replication storms during snapshot export.
diego: Yep saw that. Hot-tenant had millions of ephemeral idempotency keys in memory, snapshot tried to ship them all. OOM + replication lag.
alexa: Two short options: (1) throttled snapshot: stream per-tenant with rate-limit + compact on write (keep only most recent N keys), (2) snapshot with delta-filter: only keys newer than watermark T.
nora: I like (2) for promos where we have a neat drain-window. We can pick watermark = last-accepted-write-ts at fence time. Anything older than watermark probably already safe to expire.
diego: But clients that retry later with older idempotency keys may reapply. If we drop older keys we risk duplicates. We need a documented tradeoff: bounded window of duplicate-risk vs practicality.
alexa: What about hybrid: keep compacted per-tenant ring buffer of size M (configurable) + age TTL. For hot tenants set M smaller but bump promotion priority so their ring gets exported first. Also add per-tenant token bucket to the exporter.
sam: Implementation note: exporter sidecar can expose metrics: export_rate, export_lag_by_tenant, dumped_keys_count. Use these to abort promote if any exceed threshold.
opsbot: RUNBOOK: exporter abort if export_lag > 5m OR dumped_keys_count_for_any_tenant > 10M. See https://go.redwood/runbooks/promo-export-params
diego: For correctness labeling, add header to snapshot metadata: "contains_idempo=true, watermark_ts=...", so validator knows semantics. Validator will fail if it sees keys older than watermark are missing.
alexa: Validator job: sample K keys per-tenant (prefer recently written) and assert presence/order in target after apply. If sample fails, auto-revert. Add quick-check CLI: `rw-promote-check --tenant Y --sample 50`.
nora: For privacy, snapshot must strip payloads and retain only idempotency_key hash + seq + tenant. Use HMAC with control-plane key so raw keys not exposed in plain text.
sam: Agreed. For private deployments we should use customer KMS to HMAC. Default: platform KMS. Add audit tag when HMAC key used.
diego: Edge-case: streaming exporter may reorder keys if parallelized. Ensure compaction is commutative: reduce by key to last-seq. Use idempotency-key as partition key for compaction stage.
alexa: Also propose a soft-fallback: if exporter hits hot-tenant threshold, operator can do a targeted micro-promote: promote all other tenants first and delay the hot one until dedicated window. Less blast radius.
nora: Ops playbook note: include commands to adjust exporter token-buckets and to set tenant-specific ring-buffer sizes. We'll add to runbook and require a two-person approval for raising limits on hot tenants.
sam: I'll sketch the exporter design doc with pseudo-code for compaction and watermarking. Small snippet for compaction logic:
```
for event in stream:
  key = event.idempotency_key
  store[key] = max(store[key], event.seq)
# periodically emit compacted entries per-tenant
```
diego: Add metrics we need on the dashboard: per-tenant export_lag, compaction_rate, exported_key_count, exporter_memory_mb. Ops threshold page to alert on top-10 tenants by exported_key_count.
alexa: Communication to customers: short advisory in tenant dashboard when promote scheduled: "During promotion, we export transient dedupe metadata limited to recent window. To avoid duplicates please use idempotency-key + prefer updating to SDK vX that supports consistency-token." 
nora: Final decision summary: 1) exporter uses watermark-based delta + per-tenant ring buffer compaction, 2) hard abort thresholds and operator approval for raising limits, 3) validator sample-run before flip, 4) privacy via HMAC and TTL 72h, 5) runbook commands for micro-promote.
opsbot: Promotion job DRY-RUN created: DRY-4965432100. Notifications: ops@, infra-runtime@.
nora: Thanks all. Sam & Diego, please post the design doc link when ready and tag me for a dry-run review.
